name: cheops
why: Chess opponent simulator from logological research, exploring the statistical behaviour of the game in a niche, unusual way.

brief.what_it_is: CHEOPS (CHEss OPponent Simulator) is a chess program that supports human-vs-human, human-vs-computer, and computer-vs-computer play. It represents the board as a 64-square linear array, searches the game tree with alpha-beta, and scores positions with an evaluation function that considers material, mobility, and motif features. The homepage does not say what input or output formats it uses.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage gives no stated motivation. The scout notes describe it as a chess program from logological research that explores the statistical behaviour of the game in an unusual way, but the homepage itself does not say that.
brief.how_it_works: The board is a 64-square linear array. Move choice comes from alpha-beta game tree search. Static evaluation combines material, mobility, and motif features.
brief.install_notes: Written in ANSI C++, so it should compile with any conforming C++ compiler. A standard configure script is provided for Unix-like systems. Prebuilt binaries exist for openSUSE, and third-party Windows builds exist: Michael Yee's UCI-enabled build of 1.1, and Daniel José Queraltó's build of 1.2, which may also need Microsoft's Visual C++ runtime. The author says he takes no responsibility for the third-party packages. The homepage gives no Homebrew-specific notes.
brief.standout: It is a complete chess engine with a UCI-enabled Windows build, and its evaluation includes motif features, not just material and mobility. The homepage presents it as a fully functional program, so it is not a toy.
brief.status: Quiet. The homepage names version 1.3, released 2016-12-27, as the latest release and shows nothing newer. I did not see commit history or a dated README, so I cannot confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The homepage points to a GitHub development version, but I did not fetch the GitHub repository, so I have no details on its state. Third-party Windows builds are of older versions (1.1 and 1.2), not 1.3. Windows users may need the Visual C++ runtime. I did not read the online documentation, so the command-line interface is unverified. The homepage does not state the license beyond GPL-style free software terms.
quotes: CHEOPS (CHEss OPponent Simulator) is a fully-functional chess program capable of human-vs-human, human-vs-computer, and computer-vs-computer play.
CHEOPS is written in ANSI C++ and as such should compile on any system with a conforming C++ compiler.
CHEOPS is Free Software. It can be freely used, modified, and distributed under the terms of the GNU General Public Licence.
